assertion.statement: The same-field maximal-order CM factor Eprime has original stable height equal to the average of -log(2pi)-2log|eta(tau)|-(1/2)log Im(tau) after a good-reduction extension.
assertion.objects: The actual Eprime/L from the maximal-order quotient, with fundamental discriminant Delta_F; its individual complex embeddings.
assertion.hypotheses: Eprime is a CM elliptic curve, hence potentially everywhere good; the analytic discriminant formula applies to each embedding and the finite discriminant term vanishes on the good-reduction extension.
assertion.quantifiers: Every embedding of a field where Eprime has everywhere good reduction; average with division by its absolute degree.
assertion.parameter_range: CM elliptic curves over number fields, with reduced imaginary-quadratic periods.
assertion.uniformity: Stable height is unchanged by the auxiliary good-reduction extension, whose degree never enters the later isogeny bound.
assertion.constants: Analytic discriminant (2pi)^12 eta(tau)^24; sqrt(3)/2<=Im(tau)<=sqrt(|Delta_F|)/2.
assertion.normalizations: Original stable Faltings metric; individual-embedding equation6.2, not the class-average Proposition6.1.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No Weierstrass-coefficient condition over Q(j) is imported from Proposition6.1; the auxiliary good-reduction field is not the isogeny field L.
assertion.limit_order: Construct Eprime over L, pass to a good-reduction extension only to evaluate stable height, apply the individual formula, and return to the same L for the isogeny estimate.

preliminary_derivation.argument: If A were geometrically simple, its division endomorphism algebra acts faithfully on H1 of dimension4 and its dimension divides4. Containing B forces equality with B, which lacks a commutative semisimple subalgebra of dimension4 required by CM type. Distinct elliptic factors give a product of commutative fields, incompatible with B. A non-CM repeated factor gives M2(Q), which cannot be isomorphic to division B.

assertion.statement: The same full-marking scheme Y_Q is the entire canonical principal-level U(3) Shimura curve, with maximal-level forgetful map and canonical normalizer action; its generic coarse degree is36.
assertion.objects: All arithmetic components of Y_Q, the quaternionic type-C1 rational Hodge datum and full finite-adelic U(3) marking orbit.
assertion.hypotheses: The full representable marking scheme and its universal surface are supplied; the exact Milne Hodge-orbit, algebraic family, canonical-model and uniqueness criteria and the integral principal-polarization assertion are retained.
assertion.quantifiers: Every component and every marked geometric object of the full functor, compatibly with all automorphisms of C/Q.
assertion.parameter_range: Discriminant210, principal full level3, reflex fieldQ; both real half-planes and all unit marking multipliers.
assertion.uniformity: The comparison is for the entire Q-model and commutes with level forgetting and normalizer action.
assertion.constants: Stack degree72 and generic coarse degree36 after quotienting central signs; no extra field or level introduced.
assertion.normalizations: Compatible alternating forms have a full Q-times similitude class. The actual positive polarization representative is chosen only at the integral-object stage. Galois comparison uses algebraic torsion data, not rational Betti cohomology.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No uncorrected general implication from Milne8.14/8.17; verify the type-C1 full Hodge orbit directly. No positive-multiplier subgroup or fixed mod3 pairing value is substituted. CM and reciprocity ancestry of the canonical criterion remains a source input.
assertion.limit_order: Verify compatible forms and full Hodge orbit; match integral Tate lattices through finite torsion quotients; construct algebraic families and markings on every component; apply the exact canonical Q-model criterion and uniqueness.

output_assertion.statement: For the actual final primitive D210 form and R, its level satisfies N≤210^300 R^2 and rad(N) divides R.
output_assertion.objects: The same r_ell and primitive f, E=L(A[11]), the kernel field Q(chi), and the quadratic-kernel extension Fprime of their compositum.
output_assertion.hypotheses: E/Q is Galois with degree<2^66 and A has good reduction over E at2,3,5,7; chi is tame at odd primes with2-part conductor at most4; b restricts quadratically and normally as stated; actual local conductor equals v_p(N). Ramification/different and Artin conductor conventions are supplied.
output_assertion.quantifiers: Every rational p using an auxiliary ell different from p for the actual family.
output_assertion.parameter_range: Small primes2,3,5,7 and all p>7; no bound on the full tame ramification index is assumed.
output_assertion.uniformity: Bounds use only R and the fixed degree/character constraints, not a bounded coefficient-field degree.
output_assertion.constants: v_p(e_Fprime)≤65 for3,5,7 and≤67 for2; largest positive upper break≤136; Swan≤272; total conductor≤274<300 at small primes,≤2 above7 and0 outside support.
output_assertion.normalizations: Q(chi) is its kernel field, not value field. Full conductor includes tame and Swan terms without semisimplifying inertia.
output_assertion.exceptional_cases: Unbounded tame ramification is allowed. Separate torsion good reduction and prime-to11 isogeny argument establish the required Galois E; this connection does not assume them proved merely from the degree estimate.
output_assertion.limit_order: Construct E and the normal splitting extensions; bound wild p-part indices and upper breaks; bound the actual conductor; transfer to level via the all-prime comparison.

assertion.statement: For the two specified embeddings i,j of the same quadratic field F into B, inner conjugation gives b in B^times with j(x)=b^-1 i(x)b for every x in F; applied to j=f^-1 i_sigma f, the quasi-isogeny f b^-1 intertwines the specified F actions.
assertion.objects: The quaternion algebra B/Q=End^0_Qbar(A), abstract quadratic F and specified embeddings i:F→B and j=f^-1 i_sigma f:F→B.
assertion.hypotheses: B is the full non-CM endomorphism algebra; f:A→A_sigma is an independently supplied geometric quasi-isogeny, and i,i_sigma are the actual specified actions. The induced map i(x)→j(x) is a Q-algebra isomorphism of quadratic subfields.
assertion.quantifiers: For these embeddings there exists an invertible b implementing their specified field identification on every x.
assertion.parameter_range: Quadratic subfields of the characteristic-zero quaternion algebra B/Q.
assertion.uniformity: Existence for each pair only; no uniform degree or coherent choices in sigma.
assertion.constants: No quantitative bound is supplied.
assertion.normalizations: j=b^-1 i b and g=f b^-1; quasi-homomorphisms are rationalized Hom. Positive integer denominator clearing is a separate elementary step.
assertion.exceptional_cases: An unspecified conjugacy of unlabelled subfields is insufficient. b need not be integral. The official erratum corrects unit-group notation after separable extension; no inseparable case or deleted optional splitting-field parenthesis is used.
assertion.limit_order: Obtain f and full End=B first; conjugate the specified embeddings, then clear denominators. Same-L descent, compatibility, cocycles, Q-descent and quantitative bounds are separate.
